description: We’re a group of friends and colleagues; some of us have met before, some haven’t, joining NASA Space Apps challenge  to enjoy the hackathon together.
summary:
AndroFlame is an AI-powered interactive platform designed to transform NASA's extensive microgravity combustion research into accessible fire safety insights for future space exploration.

Our dashboard integrates NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) resources, allowing users to discover, compare, and rank combustion experiments based on materials, oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, and relevance to the International Space Station, lunar habitats, and Martian missions. An AI-powered research assistant helps users interpret experimental evidence, while SpaceFire Evolution highlights the development of space fire safety research.

To inspire new researchers, we developed Fire Dynamics Explorer and Learinng FireLab, offering engaging visualizations and hands-on exploration of NASA's FLEX and BASS-II experiments. Users can discover how fire behaves in microgravity, explore experimental conditions, and understand how observations become scientific measurements.

By combining NASA's experimental data, AI-assisted research, and interactive learning, AndroFlame makes complex combustion research accessible to scientists, engineers, and curious learners, inspiring future researchers and supporting safer human exploration of the Moon, Mars and beyond.
details:
Imagine lighting a candle on Earth. We are familiar with its teardrop shaped flame, but have you ever wondered what happens when the same candle burns in space? Without gravity driven convection, flames can behave differently, raising important questions about fire safety as humans prepare to explore the Moon, Mars, and beyond. For decades, NASA has conducted experiments to understand combustion in microgravity, generating a wealth of scientific knowledge. But how easily can we find, compare, and learn from these valuable findings?

This is where AndroFlame comes in. This is developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data. This is an AI-powered interactive dashboard designed to make NASA's combustion research easier to explore, understand, and apply to future space exploration.

Features

NASA has conducted decades of combustion experiments, generating valuable datasets across different materials, experimental conditions, and measurement techniques. However, discovering, comparing, and interpreting these resources can be challenging. AndroFlame addresses this by integrating NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) resources into a unified platform with the following features:

  • Catalog Explorer: Enables users to discover NASA combustion investigations based on materials, experimental conditions, hardware, and measurement techniques, with links to original scientific resources.
  • Coverage Matrix: Identifies experiments matching selected parameters, including oxygen concentration, pressure, airflow, and gravity conditions, while highlighting missing data and potential research gaps.
  • Compare Studies: Allows users to compare investigations side by side, examining experimental conditions, measurements, and findings to identify similarities, differences, and research opportunities.
  • Scenario Ranking: Prioritizes investigations according to their research relevance to the ISS, lunar habitats, and Martian missions, helping users identify useful evidence for different exploration environments.
  • SpaceFire Evolution: Presents the historical development of spacecraft fire safety, highlighting significant incidents, scientific discoveries, and technological advancements.
  • Beyond PSI: Extends exploration beyond the PSI repository by connecting users with additional NASA research, scientific publications, and supporting resources.
  • Fire Dynamics Explorer: Uses interactive visualizations to introduce fundamental combustion phenomena and demonstrate how physical conditions influence fire behaviour.
  • Learning FireLab: Provides a beginner-friendly virtual laboratory featuring NASA's FLEX and BASS-II investigations, allowing users to explore microgravity combustion, experimental procedures, and the transformation of observations into scientific measurements.
  • Dr. Spark: An interactive learning companion (Chatbot) designed to make space fire science more approachable, engaging, and enjoyable for newcomers.
  • ASK (AI Research Assistant): Helps users investigate scientific questions, interpret experimental evidence, and explore NASA research through AI-assisted explanations supported by source references. That offers detailed analysis compared to Dr Spark along with proper references and citations.

Together, these features connect scientific discovery, experimental comparison, AI-assisted interpretation, and interactive learning within a single research environment. For a closer look at AndroFlame and its features, please watch the guided walkthrough video available on our homepage. (https://spaceapps-flame-in-freefall.vercel.app/ )

Benefits

AndroFlame provides four key benefits to researchers, engineers, students, and the wider scientific community:

  • Simplified Research Discovery: Makes NASA's combustion investigations easier to find, filter, compare, and understand, reducing the effort required to navigate extensive scientific resources.
  • Evidence-Based Research Planning: Helps researchers identify relevant experimental conditions, recognize data limitations, and explore potential research gaps through the Coverage Matrix and Scenario Ranking along with proper references of the sources of informations.
  • Accessible Scientific Learning: Uses FireLab and Fire Dynamics Explorer to introduce complex combustion concepts through interactive experiences that encourage curiosity and scientific understanding of new researchers and students.
  • Bridging Experiments and Computational Modelling: Makes experimental conditions, measurements, and uncertainties easier to examine, supporting the interpretation of experimental findings and the development and validation of combustion models.

Ultimately, AndroFlame makes space fire research more accessible, efficient, engaging, and useful for both experienced scientists and the next generation of researchers.

Impact

We believe AndroFlame can make a meaningful difference in four areas:

  • Accelerating Scientific Research: Helping researchers find relevant NASA experiments, compare results, identify knowledge gaps, and spend more time on scientific analysis rather than searching for data.
  • Inspiring the Next Generation of Researchers: Making space fire science interesting and approachable through FireLab, Fire Dynamics Explorer, and interactive learning experiences that encourage curiosity.
  • Supporting Future Space Exploration: Helping researchers connect existing combustion evidence with fire safety challenges in spacecraft and future lunar and Martian habitats.
  • Democratizing Scientific Knowledge: Making NASA's valuable research easier to access and understand, regardless of someone's academic or professional background or experience.

Tools, Software, and Technologies

NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI): Our main data source. It gives us 24 combustion investigations (19 in microgravity, 5 on the ground or from modeling) and their experimental data tables.

NASA publications and challenge resources: NASA fact sheets, the PSI Researcher’s Guide, mission history pages (Apollo 1, Apollo 13, Mir) and NASA Spinoff pages. We use these for background and citations.

AI research assistant (ASK): Uses the open model GPT-OSS-120B, run through Groq. It explains questions using only NASA sources, cites them, and says so when the data can’t answer a question.

Smart search: Combines keyword search with meaning-based search, so you can find, filter, compare and rank experiments by fuel, oxygen level, pressure, airflow and gravity.

Website: Built with Next.js and React. It runs in any normal web browser and needs no special equipment.

Backend: Built with Python (FastAPI) and an SQLite database.

Hosting: The website is on Vercel and the backend is on Render.

Development: Code is kept on GitHub. We used an AI coding assistant (Claude) during development. For codes and details please visit:

https://github.com/Rafat001/spaceapps-flame-in-freefall

Creativity and Innovation

What makes AndroFlame different is that we did not want to build just another database or AI chatbot. We wanted users to experience the research process.

A researcher can start with a question, find relevant NASA experiments, compare experimental conditions, identify missing information, and explore what the results actually mean.

Our Scenario Ranking feature helps connect NASA's existing research with future space missions. Meanwhile, FireLab and Fire Dynamics Explorer allow newcomers to explore combustion phenomena through interactive experiences instead of relying entirely on technical papers.

We also wanted the platform to encourage critical thinking. Rather than presenting every AI-generated explanation as a scientific conclusion, AndroFlame emphasizes original NASA evidence, experimental limitations, and missing information through proper source referencing. This combination of research tools and hands-on learning is what makes our approach distinctive.

Consideration

Throughout development, we focused on four priorities:

  • Scientific Reliability: To increase the reliability of the APP we introduced proper referencing of the dataset and the publication of the researchers.
  • Accessibility: We wanted both experienced researchers and complete beginners to feel comfortable exploring the platform, without requiring specialized knowledge or equipment.
  • Cost and Affordability: By using publicly available NASA datasets and browser-based tools, we aimed to keep the platform affordable. We also considered AI usage costs to support wider access.
  • User Experience: We focused on making complex research easier to navigate and understand through clear explanations, visualizations, and interactive activities.

Our Vision

We want AndroFlame to make space fire research easier to explore, more interesting to learn, and more useful for future discoveries. By bringing NASA's experimental knowledge closer to researchers, engineers, and students, we hope to encourage new ideas and contribute to safer human exploration of the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
